nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Concerning لا there are three views. Al-Akhfash said: it is a connective (ṣila, i.e., redundant) — this is one view. It has been said: it is in the sense of ألا (the opening particle "indeed"); al-Akhfash also mentioned this. The third view is the view of the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwīl): al-Ḥasan narrated from Mujāhid, who said: «لا» is a rejection of their speech; then He began: أُقْسِمُ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, الْبَلَدِ there are three views: it is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا; it is a badal (substitute); and the most fitting is the third, that it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The grammarians mention ʿaṭf bayān in general terms, and I know of no one who explained it and the difference between it and the badal except Ibn Kaysān. He said: the difference between them is that the meaning of the badal is that you put the second in the place of the first, as though you had not mentioned the first; and the meaning of ʿaṭf bayān is that you assume that, if you mentioned the first noun alone, it would not be known except by the second, and if you mentioned the second alone, it would not be known except by the first, so you brought it to clarify the first, standing for it in the place of the naʿt and the tawkīd (emphasis). He said: the demonstration of this is in the vocative: يا أخانا زيد أقبل ("O our brother, Zayd, come forward") is on the badal, as though you had removed the first and said: يا زيد. If you intend ʿaṭf bayān, you say: يا أخانا زيدا أقبل.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (النجدين is) a second object from which إلى was omitted, on the view of the Basrans. Likewise Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 565- كما عسل الطّريق الثّعلب ("as the fox trotted along the road"): according to him, the preposition was dropped from it; according to the Kufans, it is an adverb (ẓarf) like amām and quddām (in front).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
It is said: the way of «لا» in the like of this is that it comes repeated, as in فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى [al-Qiyāma: 31]; and Sībawayh permitted it singly, and recited: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil] 566-
من صدّ عن نيرانها ... فأنا ابن قيس لا براح
(Whoever turns away from its fires — I am Ibn Qays: no retreat!)
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) disagreed with him and made this a poetic necessity (iḍṭirār). As for the verse, it has the meaning of repetition, because He, Mighty and Majestic, explained the meaning of the steep path (al-ʿaqaba) with something that is repeated. Qatāda said: the Fire is a steep path before the Garden.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t:
The implied form is: the scaling of the steep path is to free a neck (i.e., a slave), as Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: «Whoever frees a slave, Allah, Glorified, frees for every limb of it a limb of his from the Fire». Abū Hurayra said: even his private part for its private part.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ [Translator's note: the vowelling printed is the standard one; the reading of these readers is فَكَّ رَقَبَةً أَوْ أَطْعَمَ, with past verbs, as the discussion below shows]. Then the grammarians discussed this. Al-Farrāʾ chose this reading and argued that after it comes ثم كان, i.e., since كان, a past verb, is conjoined to the first, it must be «فكّ» so that a past verb is conjoined to a past verb. Al-Akhfash, Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd chose the other reading.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Religion forbids attacking the reading by which the community read, and it cannot have been taken except from the Prophet ﷺ; and he, peace be upon him, said: «The Qur'an was revealed in seven aḥruf». So they are two good readings, and neither may be put ahead of the other. As for al-Farrāʾ's objection based on كان and on conjunction with the first, it is not binding, because it is not permissible that it be conjoined according to the meaning [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense may be "because it may be conjoined according to the meaning"], since the meaning is "he did this". And he himself contradicted his statement by permitting the other reading on the implication of «أن», and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 567-
ألا أيّهذا اللّائمي أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللّذّات هل أنت مخلدي
(O you who blame me for attending the battle and for witnessing pleasures — will you make me immortal?)
He means أن أحضر; and if the matter were as he said, he would have put أحضر in the accusative. And implying «أن» is not permissible except with a compensation, because it is part of a noun.
Abū ʿUbayd objected, saying: the choice is «فكّ رقبة», because it explains the steep path. And it is reported that Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said: everything about which He, Mighty and Majestic, said وما أدراك, He has explained, and whatever He said وما يدريك about, He has not explained. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ [al-Qāriʿa: 3] and, exalted be His mention, said ما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ [al-Ḥāqqa: 3], and after this there is no explanation.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ that they read «وأطعم في يوم ذا مسغبة». Al-Farrāʾ said — although he did not mention who read «ذا مسغبة» — it is an adjective of يتيم, i.e., an orphan possessing hunger. Abū Jaʿfar said: The error in this is very clear, because an adjective may not precede the thing described, and I do not know how this occurred to him such that he mentioned it in the book «al-Maʿānī»! Rather, «ذا مسغبة» is in the accusative by أطعم, and يتيما is a badal (substitute) for it.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, i.e., he remained firm in faith; and it has been said: ثم is for (sequence in) informing. وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ: the verb and the bāʾ were repeated for emphasis (tawkīd).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: I.e., they are taken toward the right, to the Garden, and the people of the Fire toward the left, to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Al-Akhfash said: ḥill and ḥalāl (lawful), and ḥirm and ḥarām (sacred/forbidden) [Translator's note: i.e., حِلٌّ in وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ is equivalent to حلال].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: Whoever takes it from aṣada should pronounce it with hamza, and whoever takes it from awṣada may not pronounce it with hamza.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَوالِدٍ: the wāw is a conjunction (wāw ʿaṭf), not a wāw of oath, and likewise وَما وَلَدَ. Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī said:
وَوالِدٍ is Ibrāhīm ﷺ, and his child (is what he begot). It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: the father is the one who begets, and وَما وَلَدَ is his child.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is on the basis that it is general, and it seems the clearest thing that is said; and the implied form may be "by a father and his begetting", so that «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it. Among the clearest things said about its meaning is the saying of ʿAṭāʾ, who said: فِي كَبَدٍ means in struggling with affairs. Al-Ḥasan said: he struggles with prosperity and adversity, and no one struggles with affairs as the son of Adam struggles. Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said: he struggles with the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. Mujāhid said: he is a drop of fluid and a clinging clot, and he does not cease to be in struggle. These views go back to one meaning, and it is the clearest thing that has been said about it, i.e., he struggles with affairs and labours at them. This is the apparent meaning of kabad in the speech of the Arabs. Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī said: [al-Basīṭ] 563-
لي ابن عمّ لو أنّ النّاس في كبد ... لظلّ محتجرا بالنّبل يرميني
(I have a cousin who, were people in hardship, would stay girded with arrows shooting at me.)
And Labīd said: [al-Munsariḥ] 564- قمنا وقام الخصوم في كبدي
(We stood, and the adversaries stood in hardship.)

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: It has been said that by this is meant the disbeliever, i.e., does he think that Allah will not have power over him and punish him? So He, exalted be His praise, informed of his ignorance.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: It has been said: he wards off with this (saying) the doing of good deeds; and it has been said: he said this out of regret, and what comes after it indicates this answer. Abū Jaʿfar said: لبد may be the plural of lubda, and it may be a singular like ḥuṭam. It is narrated from Abū Jaʿfar (al-Qāriʾ) that he read لبّدا, the plural of lābid [Translator's note: the text reads «لا بد»], and from Mujāhid that he read لبدا (lubudan), the plural of labūd. We know of no disagreement about its meaning: that it is "much".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: The original is يرأه; the vowel of the hamza was shifted onto the rāʾ, so it took fatḥa, and the hamza fell away. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no one among the grammarians who discussed the reason why the hamza falls away (rather than remaining) when its vowel is cast onto what precedes it, except ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān; I asked him about it, and he said: when the vowel of the hamza dropped and it became quiescent, and the rāʾ before it was quiescent, it was given an accidental vowel, so its status was that of a quiescent letter, and after it was a quiescent letter, so what came after it — the hamza — was deleted.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: (The word) lisān (tongue) is treated as masculine and feminine: whoever makes it masculine forms its plural as alsina, and whoever makes it feminine says alsun. He said: and in its diminutive, lusayyin with doubled yāʾ and lusayna with it undoubled. The original of shafa (lip) is shafha, and the evidence for that is its plural, its diminutive and the derivation of the verb from it.
